battle.name: 加拉曼特斯戰爭
battle.brief: 前十九年，阿非利加行省總督科爾奈利烏斯·巴爾布斯派邦庫斯率軍深入費贊沙漠，鎮壓長期越境劫掠的加拉曼特斯人，奪其聚落十五座，迫其北撤到沙漠腹地。遠征隊以改革後的羅馬軍團為骨幹，標槍是每名步兵的標準投射兵器，出發先以騎兵搜索水源，再以盾陣進逼村莊成排投槍。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 交戰的兩方是羅馬國家與費贊的加拉曼特斯人。羅馬一方以阿非利加行省為基地，行省總督科爾奈利烏斯·巴爾布斯主持軍務，實際率隊踏沙的是將軍蓋烏斯·科爾奈利烏斯·埃米利烏斯·邦庫斯；兵種包括馬里烏斯改革後的羅馬軍團步兵、以阿非利加與高盧人為主的輔助步兵、由軍團抽調的騎兵營以及隨軍的迦太基式雙輪戰車。最高決策權在奧古斯都手上，他並未親征，只透過總督與將軍的層級下令。加拉曼特斯一方是由利比科-柏柏爾人與撒哈拉牧民混合成的部族聯盟，活動於今利比亞西南部的費贊盆地，平日逐水草而居，以劫掠、販賣俘虜與穀物維生，作戰以步兵為主，配備長矛、標槍、弓箭與短刀，另有四匹馬拉的戰車隊用於向南方獵奴。他們沒有羅馬式的常備編制與統一後勤，作戰單位是各部族自己的首領。戰前數年，羅馬邊境之外被打散的蓋圖利人逃入費贊，煽動加拉曼特斯人越境掠奪羅馬的城鎮與田莊，成為遠征的直接導火線。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the Roman state on one side and the Garamantes of the Fezzan on the other. Rome drew its forces from the province of Africa: the provincial governor Cornelius Balbus directed the military effort, while the general Gaius Cornelius Aemilius Boncus actually led the column into the sand. The order of battle included the infantry of the legion reformed by Marius, auxiliary infantry raised mainly among the peoples of Africa and Gaul, cavalry detachments drawn from the legions, and the Gallic-style two-wheeled chariots that marched with the column. Final authority lay with Augustus, who never left Rome and gave his orders through the chain of governor and general. The Garamantes were a tribal confederacy of mixed Libyco-Berber and Saharan pastoral stock, active in the Fezzan basin of what is now south-western Libya. They were nomads who moved with the grazing, living on plunder, the sale of captives and grain; in battle they fought mostly on foot, with spears, javelins, bows and short blades, and they kept teams of four-horse chariots for raiding slaves in the deep south. They had no Roman-style standing establishment and no unified logistics: each tribe fought under its own leader. In the years before the campaign, Gaetulians who had been broken up beyond the Roman frontier fled into the Fezzan and incited the Garamantes to raid Roman towns and farms, and that incitement was the direct spark of the expedition.
people: 屋大維（奧古斯都）是這場戰爭的最高統帥，但人從未離開羅馬，命令經由阿非利加行省總督科爾奈利烏斯·巴爾布斯下達；這位小巴爾布斯是家族中較年輕的一支，長期在非洲經營，深知如何以當地盟邦與輔助軍作戰。帶隊深入沙漠的是蓋烏斯·科爾奈利烏斯·埃米利烏斯·邦庫斯，他是少數真正踏進撒哈拉腹地的羅馬將領之一，據普林尼記載，他奪下加拉曼特斯人的十五座聚落。加拉曼特斯一方由一位被稱為加拉曼特斯之王的首領率領，編年史沒有留下這位首領的名字，只說遠征之後他或他的王子被送往羅馬作為人質，同時部族答應停止越境劫掠。留下戰記的還有老普林尼，他在《自然史》中記述了這場戰爭的結果，是今日能確認十五座聚落淪陷這一事實的主要來源。戰後數百年間，拉丁文獻中還能讀到其他相關人物：公元六年再度深入費贊的提米西提烏斯與倫圖盧斯·蓋圖利庫斯，以及公元二〇二年攻入首都加拉馬、終結加拉曼特斯國的塞普蒂米烏斯·塞維魯斯。加拉曼特斯之王的存在本身也是記錄的一部分，羅馬史家正是靠這類提及，才把一座遠在沙海彼端的國度寫進了地中海的世界地圖。
peopleEn: Octavian, Augustus, was the supreme commander of this war, yet he never left Rome, and his orders travelled down through the provincial governor of Africa, Cornelius Balbus. The younger Balbus, of the less senior branch of that family, had spent long years in Africa and knew well how to fight with local client troops and auxiliaries. The man who actually led the column into the desert was Gaius Cornelius Aemilius Boncus, one of the few Roman generals to penetrate the heart of the Sahara; Pliny records that he took fifteen of the Garamantian settlements. The Garamantes were led by a ruler styled their king, whose name the chroniclers did not preserve: the tradition says only that after the expedition the king, or his son, was brought to Rome as a hostage, while the tribes gave their word to stop the raids. The battle itself was also written down by Pliny the Elder, whose Natural History is the principal source for the fact of the fifteen captured settlements. In the centuries that followed, Latin literature preserved other related names: Timesitheus and Lentulus Gaetulicus, who marched deep into the Fezzan again in the sixth year of our era, and Septimius Severus, who stormed the capital of Garama in AD 202 and ended the Garamantian state. The Garamantian king is himself part of the record: it was precisely through references to men like him that Roman historians placed a kingdom at the far end of the sand on the mental map of the Mediterranean.
kits: 這場戰爭的技術核心是羅馬標槍。改革後的羅馬軍團以標槍作為步兵的主要投射兵器：槍身中空，前端接一截鐵製槍頸（amentum），鐵頸約重一公斤；投出後鐵頸容易彎折，釘在盾牌上時會把盾牌拽歪，敵人難以自行拔出，盾手只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。有效投擲距離約三十公尺，正好落在投射兵器交火與短兵相接之間。輔助軍的標槍比軍團的略短、略輕，非洲本地徵召的步兵另備更小的標槍。羅馬隊伍還配備皮盾（scutum）、短劍（gladius）、長矛（hasta）、皮兜投石索（fustor），以及從巴利阿里群島與北非抽調的弓手；騎兵營與戰車隊則使用長矛與標槍。敵方裝備以木柄標槍、弓箭、長矛與短刀為主，工藝與冶金能力卻不弱，費贊先民懂得挖掘地下引水渠（foggara），把地下水引到地表的聚落，並燒製陶器與鍛打鐵器。運輸端，加拉曼特斯人靠駱駝，羅馬遠征隊則攜帶帳篷、水袋、木桶、備用標槍與軍糧，並沿途尋找古井與前人驛站；羅馬的沙路里程碑與井址記錄，也是在這些年裡開始出現的。
kitsEn: The technical heart of this war was the Roman pilum. After Marius's reform the legion took the pilum as its principal missile: the shaft is hollow and carries an iron neck (amentum) of roughly one kilogram at the front. Once thrown, the iron shank tends to bend, and when it lodges in a shield it drags the shield out of line, so the enemy cannot pull it free and must withdraw behind cover with half a spear still in his hands. Its effective throwing range is about thirty metres, exactly the band between missile exchange and hand-to-hand fighting. Auxiliary troops carried shorter and lighter pila than the legion did, and locally raised African infantry bore smaller versions still. The Roman order of battle also included the scutum, the gladius, the hasta, the leather-sling fustor, and archers drawn from the Balearic islands and North Africa; cavalry and chariot units used the lance and the pilum. The enemy fought with wooden-shafted javelins, bows, spears and short blades, but their craft and metallurgy were not backward: the Fezzan people knew how to dig foggara, underground channels that brought groundwater to the surface settlements, and they fired pottery and worked iron. On the logistic side the Garamantes relied on the camel, while the Roman column carried tents, water skins, wooden barrels, spare pila and rations, and searched along the route for old wells and the stations of earlier travellers; the milestone markers and well-heads of the Roman desert road also begin to appear from these years onward.
tactics: 羅馬遠征隊以縱隊行軍，騎兵營在前方搜索方圓數里的水源與村落，步兵縱隊之間夾著載給養的牲畜與輜重車，抵達聚落外圍即先立營紮寨取水，再依序攻取。費贊的村莊多為土坯牆與圍牆的堡壘式聚落，進攻時先用投石手與弓手壓制牆頭，步兵結成密集盾陣向前推進，把標槍成排擲過城牆或屋頂，壓住守軍的射擊窗口，再由雲梯與突門突破；標槍一旦釘在牆頭守軍的盾牌上，守軍便無法迅速重新舉盾射箭。加拉曼特斯人沒有遠射優勢，只能靠城頭拋石與短兵相接，抵抗往往集中於最堅固的幾座聚落。羅軍的關鍵不在一次殲滅，而在切斷部族聯盟的遊動補給：奪下一座聚落，就等於奪走其水井、穀倉、陶窯與人頭稅的來源，逼得該支部族退往更深的沙漠。奪城之後羅馬留駐守備與代理人，組織下一次推進時則依靠對水源與道路的掌握。沙漠行軍本身是一場耐力競賽：每人每日需水數公升，行程必須對準井位，否則非戰減員會超過戰鬥減員。
tacticsEn: The Roman column marched in line of column, with a cavalry detachment searching ahead for water and villages within several miles, the infantry formations separated by draught animals and baggage wagons carrying supply, and the whole force first pitching camp and drawing water outside a settlement before attempting it in turn. The villages of the Fezzan were mostly fortified places of mud brick and enclosure wall. In the attack, slingers and archers first silenced the ramparts, the infantry advanced in a dense shield wall and threw the pila in volleys over the wall or across the roofs to shut the defenders' firing loopholes, and only then did ladders and breaches open the way. A pilum that stuck in a defender's shield on the rampart left him unable to raise the shield and shoot again in good order. The Garamantes had no long-range advantage; they could only throw stones from the wall and fight at close quarters, and their resistance usually centred on the strongest of the settlements. The key to the Roman method was not annihilation but the severing of the nomadic confederacy's mobile supply: taking one settlement meant taking its well, its granary, its potteries and the source of its tribute, and the tribe was pushed deeper into the desert. After the capture the Romans left garrisons and proxies behind, and any later advance depended on control of water and roads. Desert marching was itself a contest of endurance: a man needed several litres of water a day, the route had to be keyed to the wells, and losses from thirst could easily outnumber losses in battle.
data: 可核實的數字不多，但有幾項相當可靠。年份是公元前三方十九年，即屋大維掌權的第十八年；戰役發生在春季到初夏的開季，羅馬遠征隊通常在雨季結束後出發，趕在盛夏之前完成主要戰鬥。普林尼《自然史》記載羅馬方面奪取加拉曼特斯聚落十五座，這是史籍為這場戰爭留下的唯一確數戰果。距離方面，從羅馬非洲行省的據點大萊普提斯到首都加拉馬，公路與駱駝道合計超過一千公里，途中多為無水的沙海與鹽灘，羅軍以每日二十至三十公里的速度推進，一支隊伍需要走上一個多月。武器細節可由波利比奧與其他古代作家推得：標槍槍身中空，前端接一截約一公斤重的鐵矛頭，槍尾加配重球以利投擲；投擲距離約三十公尺。軍團規模約五千至六千人，輔助軍由數百至上千人構成，遠征總兵力應在數千人至一萬人之間，但流傳下來的文獻沒有留下確切數字。羅馬的戰果也顯示這是一場克制的懲罰性遠征：敵國主體未毀，加拉馬斯本身直到公元二〇二年才被塞維魯斯攻陷。
dataEn: Verifiable figures are few, but several are solid. The year is nineteen BC, the eighteenth year of Octavian's ascendancy; the campaign fell in the opening season between spring and early summer, Roman columns normally setting out once the rains were over and completing the main fighting before the height of the heat. Pliny's Natural History records that the Romans took fifteen Garamantian settlements, and this is the one exact result the ancient literature preserves for the war. On distance: from the Roman base at Leptis Magna in the province of Africa to the capital at Garama, the road and the caravan track together run more than a thousand kilometres, through stretches of waterless sand and salt flats. The Romans advanced at twenty to thirty kilometres a day, so a column needed well over a month on the move. The details of the weapon can be reconstructed from Polybius and other ancient writers: the shaft of the pilum is hollow and carries an iron head of about one kilogram at the front, with a weighted butt to make the throw work, and it is thrown to about thirty metres. A legion numbered roughly five to six thousand men and the auxiliaries from several hundred to a thousand each, so the expedition must have numbered in the thousands and perhaps up to ten thousand, but no exact figure survives in the literature. The outcome also shows this to have been a measured, punitive expedition: the enemy state was not destroyed, and Garama itself did not fall until Severus took it in AD 202.
cause: 戰爭的直接原因是連續數十年的邊境掠奪。加拉曼特斯人從費贊向地中海沿岸出擊，劫掠羅馬的城鎮、田莊與商隊，把羅馬公民帶回沙漠，轉為奴隸出售；羅馬行省的莊園、鹽場與穀物外運線因此不斷受威脅。第二層原因是利益：費贊是跨撒哈拉商路的西端轉運點，金屬、象牙、鴕鳥毛與撒哈拉以南的俘虜都經過這裡，羅馬需要把它變成可控的貿易與稅源，而不是任由游牧部族自由去留。第三層原因是蓋圖利人的煽動與羅馬邊境政策的連鎖反應：被打散的蓋圖利人躲入費贊，鼓動加拉曼特斯人出擊；阿非利加行省在奧古斯都整頓下要清除邊境騷擾，於是決定把戰線推入沙漠，把威脅的來源消滅在原地，而不是年年追擊。最後一點是屋大維整體的帝國政策：掌握北非的糧食產區與奴隸通道，羅馬的城市麵包供應與地中海秩序才能維持下去。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the war was a decade of border raiding. The Garamantes struck out of the Fezzan against the Mediterranean coast, raiding Roman towns, farms and caravans, and carrying Roman citizens back into the desert to be sold as slaves; the estates, salt works and grain-export routes of the province were therefore under constant threat. The second layer of cause is profit: the Fezzan was the western transposing point of the trans-Saharan trade, through which metal, ivory, ostrich feathers and captives from beyond the desert passed, and Rome needed to turn it into a controllable source of trade and tax rather than leave it at the disposal of roaming tribes. The third layer is the incitement of the Gaetulians and the knock-on effect of Roman frontier policy: Gaetulians broken up beyond the frontier sheltered in the Fezzan and urged the Garamantes to strike; and the province of Africa, being tidied up under Augustus, resolved to push the line of war into the desert and destroy the source of the trouble on the spot instead of chasing raiders year after year. The last cause lies in Augustus's general imperial policy: only by holding the grain lands of North Africa and the channels of the slave trade could the bread supply of the Roman cities and the order of the Mediterranean be kept in place.
impact: 這場遠征的短期效果是明確的：加拉曼特斯人北撤，劫掠暫停，羅馬的非洲邊境在屋大維時代得以安寧。長期看，羅馬並沒有就此罷手，反而把費贊變成有制度的前線：公元一至二世紀，羅馬在通往沙漠的路線上陸續設立驛站、井與小型駐軍，加拉馬斯一帶出現常駐的羅馬據點與紀念銘文，跨撒哈拉商路被納入門戶稅與護衛制度。這條線最終通向公元二〇二年塞普蒂米烏斯·塞維魯斯攻陷加拉馬斯、拆散加拉曼特斯國的結局。經濟上，奴隸與穀物的來源從游牧劫掠轉為受監管的商隊交易，羅馬的北非行省因此得以穩定地供應城市糧食。戰術上，這次遠征也留下兩個教訓：一是沙漠遠征的致命問題是水與行程計算，而非正面戰鬥，公元六年的更深遠征因此損失大批人馬；二是羅馬遠征隊一旦奪下聚落，就會立刻把它改造成後續遠征的落腳點，戰果因此得以累積。史料上，編年史、普林尼的《自然史》與後世銘文構成了這段沙漠戰事唯一而珍貴的文字記錄。
impactEn: The effect of the expedition was clear in the short run: the Garamantes withdrew north, the raids stopped, and the African frontier enjoyed quiet under Augustus. In the long run Rome did not stop there but turned the Fezzan into an ordered frontier: through the first and second centuries AD the Romans laid out stations, wells and small garrisons along the road into the desert, permanent Roman posts and dedicatory inscriptions appeared around Garama, and the trans-Saharan trade was drawn into a system of customs and armed escort. That line of posts eventually runs to AD 202, when Septimius Severus took Garama and broke up the Garamantian state. Economically, the source of slaves and grain shifted from nomadic plunder to supervised caravan trade, and the province of Africa could supply the cities with food on a regular basis. Tactically the expedition left two lessons: the killer problem in a desert campaign is water and the calculation of the march, not the frontal clash, and the far deeper expedition of AD 6 lost a great many men for that reason; and once a Roman column took a settlement it turned it at once into the staging point for the next advance, so results accumulated. As sources, the chronicles, Pliny's Natural History and the later inscriptions constitute the only precious written record of this desert war.
result: 結果是有限但實在的勝利。邦庫斯率軍深入費贊，奪取加拉曼特斯聚落十五座，迫使部族聯盟退往沙漠深處，首領或王子被送至羅馬，成為約束部族的抵押。掠奪在若干年內停止，羅馬的非洲邊界換來一段可以重建的時間，代價則是一支深入沙海數週、消耗大量水與糧的遠征隊。結果沒有更徹底，是因為遠征的目標本來就是解除邊境壓力而不是消滅一個國家：加拉曼特斯國繼續存在，首都加拉馬斯依舊是撒哈拉商路的樞紐，直到公元二〇二年才被塞普蒂米烏斯·塞維魯斯攻陷，加拉曼特斯王國從此解體。對武器史而言，這場戰爭留下的是羅馬標槍在帝國邊疆的一次實戰檢驗：投射兵器配合盾陣、騎兵搜索與縱隊補給，能把游牧部族的襲擊壓回沙漠，卻無法取代水源與道路所具有的政治作用。
resultEn: The result was a limited but solid victory. Boncus led his column deep into the Fezzan, took fifteen Garamantian settlements, drove the tribal confederacy back into the depths of the desert, and sent the ruler, or the ruler's son, to Rome as a pledge binding the tribes. The raids stopped for a number of years, and the Roman African frontier bought the time it needed to rebuild, at the cost of a column that spent weeks in the sand and consumed a great deal of water and grain. The result was not more complete because the aim of the expedition had never been to destroy a state but to relieve the frontier: the Garamantian kingdom continued to exist, and Garama remained the pivot of the Saharan trade until Septimius Severus stormed it in AD 202 and the kingdom came apart. In the history of weapons, what this war offers is a field test of the Roman pilum on the edge of the empire: missiles combined with the shield wall, cavalry scouting and a column disciplined in supply could push nomadic raids back into the desert, but they could not replace the political work done by water and roads.
